counts.note: canonical memories (SQL) vs vector points (Qdrant) vs chunks are counted separately; the workload is memory-only, so the chunk family is 0 and its collection may not exist

ingest.method: rows + durable upsert intents committed in batches of 100; embedding performed by the real outbox drain (drain_once → drain_pending, batch 50); nothing acks the intents on the write path, so every point in the store came through it

startup.note: this run's own open+first recall: the same store just wrote every point, so the page cache is warm. The cold-PROCESS measurement is the --reuse run (recorded under cold_process).

latency_ms.method: nearest-rank percentile over per-call wall time (time.perf_counter around one MemoryRetriever.recall call, SQL session acquisition excluded)

warm_recall.note: second pass in the SAME process: page cache warm by construction

concurrent.recall_errors_note: typed failures (e.g. IndexFreshnessTimeout) are real 503s from the freshness barrier, recorded, never dropped

latency_ms.method: nearest-rank percentile over per-call wall time (time.perf_counter around one MemoryRetriever.recall call, SQL session acquisition excluded)

gate.metric: p95 of sequential recall calls while ingest/correct/forget run
gate.authority: D4 (signed): p95 <= 150ms — RECORDED here, no assert, no code path depends on it

backup.method: PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) → file copy of the SQLite db + the embedded-Qdrant folder → copy back into a fresh dir → re-open (sqlite3 + QdrantClient) and count. Restore timing INCLUDES the verification reads.

rss.method: resource.getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss (peak, process-wide, CONTAMINATED by everything the process loaded before the stores) + ps -o rss= at measurement time (current)

outbox.note: acked = status 'done'; the write path acks its own intent, this run's ingest never did, so 'acked' here is the drain's own accounting
